To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
{e}^{x}-{e}^{4}=0
$$

First, we isolate the term with the variable exponent by adding ${e}^{4}$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}-{e}^{4} & =0 \\ {e}^{x}-\cancel{{e}^{4}}+\cancel{{e}^{4}} & =0+{e}^{4} \\ {e}^{x} & ={e}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base $e$, we equate the exponents. This gives

$$
x=4.
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=4.$
